full-song-name-collision.spec.ts.why: a `d2:` label collides with the name the unlabelled track below it would be given (#1667). The row SOURCE de-duplicates by that name, so the collision deletes a lane rather than repeating one — a missing row is invisible in a unit test of the names, and only the running app shows how many lanes the arrangement actually draws. Same for a `//`-commented copy of a named track above the live one (#1673): the row it kept was the comment's. And for a TRAILING `_` mute marker (#1679): `$_:` twice lost a row, and `drums_:` showed as a playing track. And (#1678) an unnamed track under a commented one read `d1` in the Mixer and `d2` on the timeline.

roll-opens-on-notes.spec.ts.why: The piano roll opens on its notes (#1850): centred when they fit the view, else the lowest note at the bottom; also when the pattern was read with the drawer closed; an edit never moves the view, a new statement re-opens on its own notes. Before, every roll opened at its top row with its lowest note out of view.

pattern-stack-repeats.spec.ts.why: A comma pattern whose parts are written over different numbers of bars (#1849): `<[bd ~ bd ~] [bd ~ ~ bd]>, ~ sd ~ sd, hh*8` opens editable instead of 44 of 48 cells locked, the one-bar parts are drawn as repeats in bar 2, and a click in a repeat edits the written bar so the text changes once and the grid shows both bars changed. Pins that the grid agrees with the text after the click, which a panel keeping its own edited model did not.

pattern-exact-grid.spec.ts.why: Exact grid mode (#1855), the default: each part of a comma pattern is drawn at its own steps (`~ sd ~ sd, hh*8` shows the snare as 4 boxes, each over two hat cells) and a click fills one whole own step, so the cells LCM locks on a coarser part (#1853) write the part's own spelling. Pins box count and alignment, the whole-step write in one bar only, keys stepping over a box, the Settings › Grid switch redrawing an open grid both ways, and LCM unchanged as the control.

pattern-side-toggle.spec.ts.why: collected by the gate — it runs the whole chromium project

pattern-step-lines.spec.ts.why: Stage 1 of the pattern grid (#1841): both grids draw a line where each step as written begins, and a ruler counting those steps, from the regions the parser already records. Pins line positions, that a plain column draws none, that a bar line differs from a step line, and that the sequencer's ruler follows the cursor row when parts split the bar differently.

sequencer-erase-refusal.spec.ts.why: A lit sequencer cell whose erase the writer refuses must say so: inert and titled for the pointer, and reported as a warning for a key, which never sees a title (#1836). Before, every lit cell looked clickable and 285 of the corpus's erase clicks did nothing silently.

sequencer-velocity-writable.spec.ts.why: The sequencer offers a velocity drag only where the gain writer writes it (#1839). Its own copy of the writer's rule missed the leaf line, so on 20 leaf-read corpus grids a drag redrew the bar and never changed the code.

roll-move-decline-reported.spec.ts.why: A move drop the writer declines must be reported and must leave the note at the last accepted frame (#1452). The message existed and was unreachable for this whole class; nothing was looking, which is why it survived. Both outcome clauses are pinned because a declined drop rests in two different places.
